comparison.text: Live with this air permanently and it prices out at about 4 years of life expectancy. That is the math, not a mood.
comparison.source_name: AQLI methodology (Ebenstein et al. 2017), University of Chicago EPIC
comparison.caveat: The AQLI conversion (0.98 years per 10 ug/m3) applies to sustained lifetime exposure, so this is what today's level would cost if it were your permanent normal, not the cost of one bad day.

comparison.text: Outdoor air pollution causes about 4.2 million early deaths a year worldwide, says WHO. It is one of the biggest killers nobody posts about.
comparison.source_name: WHO fact sheet, Ambient (outdoor) air quality and health (2019 estimate)
comparison.caveat: A modeled global estimate for 2019, the latest WHO headline figure, with uncertainty in the millions.

comparison.text: The most polluted city on Earth in the 2025 IQAir report is Loni, in Delhi NCR: 112.5 ug/m3 average, 22x the WHO limit. All 25 worst cities were in India, Pakistan and China.
comparison.source_name: IQAir, 2025 World Air Quality Report press release
comparison.caveat: IQAir rankings blend government and low-cost sensor data and only cover cities that measure at all. Plenty of unmonitored places never make the list.

comparison.text: A NIOSH N95 removes at least 95 percent of airborne particles when it seals to your face. On days like this, it is not paranoia, it is arithmetic.
comparison.source_name: CDC NIOSH, Proper N95 Respirator Use (Science Bulletin)
comparison.caveat: The 95 percent is the certified filter performance with a proper seal. Beards, gaps and surgical masks do not deliver it.

comparison.text: A week of air like this = 5.5 cigarettes. Your lungs are keeping the receipts.
comparison.source_name: Berkeley Earth, Air Pollution and Cigarette Equivalence
comparison.caveat: Extends the Berkeley Earth per-day rule of thumb across a week at the same level. Real weeks vary day to day.
